label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is sql containing user-provided cookie value decoded and passed through Base64 encode/decode (which preserves the original string), then concatenated into SQL and potentially rendered to response in error handlers. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-TP — resolved sink value is sql = "SELECT * from USERS where USERNAME='foo' and PASSWORD='" + bar + "'", where bar = param (decoded cookie value). User input flows directly to SQL string without parameterization. Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities.

evidence.note: User cookie value extracted and decoded into param variable
doSomething method passes param through Base64 encode/decode (preserves original value) to bar
SQL injection sink: bar (containing user input) concatenated directly into SQL query string
XSS sink: sql string (containing user input) passed to encodeForHTML and printed to response in error handler
